root_idea.summary: The supplied lexical evidence centers on quaking or shuddering that affects the skin, with related extensions to roughness and drying or contraction.
root_idea.development: The bodily tremor sense is accompanied by usages for skin drying, the contraction and drought-marked appearance of earth, and a year becoming drought-stricken; related derived nouns and adjectives describe the tremor or a person experiencing it.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form IV perfect citation form.

senses.definition: To shiver or shudder, with a tremor rising over the skin.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence, it is used of the skins of those who fear their Lord; the supplied form is an imperfect active verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tremor, quaking, or quivering of the skin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for the tremor that seizes or overtakes the skin.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the skin, to dry up from mange or scab.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in a construction describing the skin as drying because of mange or scab.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the earth, to become dust- or ash-coloured and contract through drought; of a year, to become a year of drought.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The year usage is reported as a figurative or extended expression; the earth usage includes both the colour change and contraction caused by drought.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rough to the touch; in a reported usage, rough and advanced in years.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description; the combination of roughness with advanced age is reported as an alternative usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person whose skin is quaking or shuddering.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active participial adjective describing someone in the state of bodily shuddering; its plural is قَشَاعِرُ.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Bodily and cutaneous quaking is represented in the Quranic verb sense.
The mange- or scab-related drying of skin is represented separately.
The drought-related colour change and contraction of earth are represented.
The drought-stricken year usage is included in the same drought extension.
The noun for a skin tremor is represented under its own headword.
The rough or rough-and-aged adjectival usage is represented.
The participial adjective for a person undergoing skin shuddering is represented.

cautions: No Maqāyīs entry was supplied; the root-level orientation is therefore limited to the supplied Lane and Mufradāt evidence.
